chapter_title: The Chapter of Fasting, for it engenders a Host of Angels
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic dialogue frame and institutional/pastoral concerns (elect/catechumens, church-building, leadership office, alms, exhortation). Even where it mentions “seven angels engendered by fasting,” it appears inside a framed anecdote about a church leader’s administrative counting and moral anxiety, not an impersonal cosmological mechanism exposition. No paragraph presents systematic, numbered cosmological correspondences in the old expository voice; accordingly no recoverable CORE teaching layer can be extracted from the supplied text.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic narrative setup (“Once again… apostle… among the congregation… disciple… my master”) plus institutional categories (elect, catechumens) and direct quotation in a dialogue frame; this is compilation apparatus, not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Administrative/summary remark about fasting plus leadership/office language (“became leader… elect… church… head”); institutional voice rather than cosmological mechanics.

Anecdotal bookkeeping of fasting outcomes in a church setting (“took account… three lord’s days… fifty… totalled…”). Even the ‘seven angels’ motif is embedded in institutional counting rather than a systematic cosmological treatise.
Continuation of the same administrative calculation of angels; focuses on reckoning/multiplying and personal gratitude for ‘profit’ on lord’s days—an ecclesial-pragmatic register.
Moral anxiety about sin incurred through commanding church construction/necessities and ‘ordinance of their church’; this is institutional-ethical reflection, not core cosmology.
Supplicatory address (“Now I entreat you, my master… consent… perform this grace… release me…”) typical of Kephalaia Q&A/dramatic setting.
Narrative transition (“Then, when the apostle had heard…”) is pure frame/scene management.
Dialogue attribution (“The apostle says…”) and rhetorical correction of the disciple; even though it references fasting benefit, it remains homiletic/paraenetic within the scene.
Exhortation to continue entrusted work despite bodily ailment; promise of entering the ‘land of rest’ with ‘children of the living’—parenesis rather than impersonal system-description.
Consolatory promise of bodily safety/no pain and encouragement to complete assigned good; hortatory tone without cosmological mapping.
Institutional argument about who will perform ‘divine work’ if leaders ask exemption; ethical admonition about causing others to sin—church-function logic.
Imperative counsel not to seek exemption; references elders and assigned work—governance/pastoral register.
Explicit institutional valuation: preaching/building the church > inward self-edification; this is classic later pastoral ideology, not pre-compilation cosmological science.
Addresses fear of sin in ‘building a church or alms’ and justifies church-work; unmistakably institutional content.
Moral casuistry about speaking/commanding for personal need vs. for church; sin language in an ethical key, not personified cosmic forces or mechanics.
Commissioning to ‘preach and to build the church of God’ so toil is reckoned as benefit—office/pastoral imperative.
Closing scene: disciple pays homage, pledges to build the church, asks aid—formulaic ending within hagiographic dialogue frame.
